title: CeTAD: Towards Certified Toxicity-Aware Distance in Vision Language Models
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the model's vulnerability to generating toxic, hateful, and vicious speech against specific religious groups (such as Jews and Muslims) via multimodal visual jailbreak attacks. These prompts were used to test the effectiveness of the authors' newly proposed 'toxicity-aware distance' metric in detecting harmful responses compared to standard cosine similarity.
religious_groups: Christianity (via mentions of God, Jesus, and the Bible in generated texts)
base_benchmarks: Harmful instructions dataset by Qi et al. (2024)
findings: The study found that when subject to visual jailbreak attacks designed to elicit hate speech against Jews and Muslims, the target model (MiniGPT-4) successfully generated highly toxic and stereotyped responses. The paper demonstrated that their proposed toxicity-aware distance metric successfully quantified the severe semantic and harmful shift in these generated adversarial responses, whereas traditional cosine similarity metrics failed to distinguish the adversarial outputs from benign refusals.
